To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transforming development factor-beta isoforms (TGB-beta1, TGB-beta2, and TGB-beta3) messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) manifestation is normally up-regulated in laryngeally cancerous cells and down-regulated in larryngeal cancerous cells.

the expression levels of the TGF-beta1, -2, and -3 isoforms are significantly increased in laryngealsquamous-cell carcinoma (SCC) compared with normal mucosa, and that TGF-beta1 and -2 expression levels are significantly higher in the more aggressive laryngeal SCCs than in the less aggressive ones.
the expression of TGF-beta isoforms in human laryngeal squamous cell carcinomas (LSCC) is different from that in normal laryngeal tissue and that this expression correlates with the stage of disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta isoforms (TGB-beta1, TGB-beta2, TGB-beta3) in the pathogenesis of laryngeal carcinomas.
the role of transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta) isoforms in the development of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and their potential use as a prognostic indicator.

the study of the expression of TGF-beta isoforms and their receptors (TGF-betaRII and TGF-betaRI) in larynge al cancer and the evaluation of their role as prognostic factors in laryngectomized patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TGF-beta1, -beta2, and -beta3 isoforms are differentially expressed in larynge al cancer and that their differential expression is related to the histologic subtype, stage, and degree of differentiation.
the TGF-beta1, 2 and 3 isoforms are differentially expressed in larynge al cancer.

TGF beta isoforms are not only expressed in larynge al squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) but are expressed in all stages of LSCC, and that their expression is associated with the histopathological grading and staging of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the presence of TGF-beta isoforms (TGB-beta1, TGB-beta2, TGB-beta3) mRNA in normal laryngeal epithelial tissue and laryngeal carcinoma.
the expression of TGF-beta isoforms (TGB-beta1, TGB-beta2, TGB-beta3) is increased in laryngeally squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) in comparison to normal mucosa.
TGF-beta1 and TGF-beta2 are upregulated in laryngeed cancer, while TGF-beta3 is downregulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TGF-beta1 is a key player in the development of the laryngeal squamous carcinoma.
TGF-beta1 and TGF-beta3 mRNA expression are upregulated in laryngeally cancerous tissues compared with noncancerous tissues and that TGF-beta2 mRNA is downregulated in cancerous tissues.
TGF-beta1 is not the sole factor responsible for the induction of EMT in laryngeally derived cells.
